newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares flat, Pacific Andes disappoints.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares flat, Pacific Andes disappoints.

text.p: The Singapore share market continued to drag its feet in early Friday trading with the bulk of volume contributed by block deals.
Frozen seafood trader Pacific Andes made a disappointing debut, falling below its initial public offer price of US$0.57.
After an hour of trading, Pacific Andes was at US$0.53. Its volume of 4.09 million shares included block trades totalling 800,000 shares at US$0.57 each.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index was off 0.55 point at 2,150.21. Market volume was 20.5 million shares with gainers leading losers by 77 to 50 and 85 issues unchanged.
"The market has been dominated by crossed trades for most of this week. Malaysian shares, which were doing well yesterday, have not really warmed up yet," said a dealer.

Dairy Farm saw 1.383 million shares crossed between US$0.573 and US$0.58. Jardine Strategic had 1.0685 million shares crossed at US$3.231 and US$3.242. Malaysia's Magnum Corp had 1.15 million shares crossed at various prices.
Malaysian over-the-counter stock DCB Holding led gainers with a S$0.25 (US$0.18) rise to S$5.15 on 151,000 shares. Singapore's City Development and Singapore Press foreign were lower.
